claims.text: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi can serve as an initially single-phase, homogeneous solid solution.
The initial CoCrFeMnNi microstructure is coarse-grained.
Single-phase FCC high- and medium-entropy alloys can undergo a rapid decrease in ductility between 400 and 800°C.
Combined elevated-temperature and high-strain-rate loading causes severe plastic deformation that dynamically refines CoCrFeMnNi grains.
The intervention produces a localized nanocrystalline layer containing high-angle grain boundaries with grain sizes of 10–50 nm.
The dynamically formed grain boundaries lack significant stabilizing segregation.
CoCrFeMnNi has a relatively high calculated average high-angle grain-boundary energy of about 0.87 J/m² at 300 K.
High grain-boundary energy corresponds to reduced boundary cohesion and a greater propensity for cohesive failure.
Below a critical grain size, dislocation activity is suppressed.
Below the critical grain size, grain-boundary sliding becomes the dominant deformation mechanism.
Solid-solution CoCrFeMnNi may undergo grain-boundary decohesion without significant segregation or phase separation.
Cavitation and intergranular decohesion at high-angle grain boundaries lead to brittle failure.
The proposed segregation-free boundary-decohesion mechanism is distinct from segregation-driven embrittlement in conventional alloys.
Relative to room-temperature, low-strain-rate loading, elevated-temperature, high-strain-rate loading reduces both ductility and fracture toughness.
The intervention causes early intergranular crack initiation and brittle fracture.
At room temperature and low strain rate, the same alloy undergoes uniform deformation and ductile fracture without significant grain refinement or intergranular decohesion.
The proposed mechanism is limited to high-temperature, high-strain-rate loading in inert environments.
Segregation or phase separation can alter grain-boundary energy and the route to decohesion.
Dynamic recrystallization or local amorphization may compete with the proposed embrittlement mechanism and alter its onset.
